title: Spots of time
hook: a lost boy, letters carved in the turf, a girl in the wind: moments that keep renewing us (The Prelude, book 12)
tomorrow: a tiger and a lamb. could the same hand have made both?

segments.voice: Yesterday, trailing clouds of glory: children arriving from God, heaven still around them, and the light fading into common day. Today, the moments that don't fade.
screen: `TRAILING CLOUDS OF GLORY.` → `MOMENTS THAT DON'T FADE.`

segments.voice: Some memories show up uninvited, as sharp as the day they happened. Wordsworth said certain ones do something strange. In The Prelude, the long poem of his own growing up, he writes: "There are in our existence spots of time, / That with distinct pre-eminence retain / A renovating virtue". Renovating: they repair us. Then he tells the one he means. As a small boy riding in the hills, he lost his guide and came down alone to a place where a murderer had once been hanged. The gallows had rotted away. Only letters, carved in the turf, remained.
screen: `MEMORIES THAT SHOW UP UNINVITED.` → `A RENOVATING VIRTUE.` → `A LOST BOY.` → `LETTERS IN THE TURF.`

segments.voice: Frightened, he climbed away, and saw only plain things: a bare pool, a beacon on the hilltop, and a girl with a pitcher on her head, forcing her way against the wind. That's all. Nothing happened. And yet the scene stayed, he says, with a visionary dreariness. Later, he came back to that same place in the happy days of early love, and the dreary spot gave him strength and radiance. So do moments like that heal you, or haunt you? Readers of The Prelude argue it two ways, and Wordsworth gives both sides their lines. Side one: the power is in the moment. The spot retains a virtue, something given, like grace, that you didn't make and can't manufacture. You can only receive it, and be grateful. Side two: the power is in the mind returning. Wordsworth also says these moments show that "The mind is lord and master", with the senses as its servant. The scene itself was bleak. The mind, coming back to it changed, made it shine. That's the teaching The Prelude leaves us: the past isn't fixed. A moment that came as fear can come back as strength, because of what it held, or because of who returns to it, or both.
screen: `A POOL, A BEACON, A GIRL IN THE WIND.` · `GIVEN: THE POWER IS IN THE MOMENT.` · `MADE: THE MIND IS LORD AND MASTER.` · `FEAR CAME BACK AS STRENGTH.` · then, large: `SPOTS OF TIME.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and, in one line, write down a moment that keeps coming back to you: not the big event, just the scene, a road, a light, a face. For two minutes, look at the line and ask what it has done for you, healed or haunted, or both.
Spots of time: Wordsworth's name, in The Prelude, for moments that stay with us and keep renewing us, even the dreary ones.
Your line: spots of time, and the mind that keeps returning to them. On we go.
